AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Zinc transporter 8 protein (ZnT8) is a transmembranic protein organizing the zinc transfer to insulin vesicles. Antibodies formed against ZnT8 (ZnT8A) are regarded as an independent autoimmunity demonstrator in type 1 diabetes (T1D) diagnosis Investigation of ZnT8ab prevalence in Turkish children with new onset T1D was planned in this study.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: 84 patients between 1-18 years of age diagnosed with T1D between February 2015- March 2016 and the control group consisting of 50 healthy children without any autoimmune diseases were included in the study. Serum samples for ZnT8A level were taken from the patient group in a week after diagnosis the latest and studied with ELISA method.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: ZnT8A positivity was detected in 58% of the patients with new onset T1D and 8% of the control group. ZnT8A positivity was shown in 7 out of 15 patients with negative results for other diabetes antibodies (ICAA, GADA or IAA). No connection was found between ZnT8A positivity and age, gender, presence or degree of ketoacidosis present during presentation, HbA1C, insulin or c-peptide level, thyroid autoantibodies or celiac antibody presence.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: ZnT8A prevalence in children with T1D in Turkey was compatible with the data from most countries. The ratio of patients who are clinically considered to have T1D but have negative routine diabetes auto-antibodies were observed to decrease nearly by 50% when ZnT8 was added to the panel. ZnT8 measurement should be more widespread for clarifying the etiology in T1D.

Article.ArticleTitle: PREVALENCE OF ZnT8 ANTIBODY IN TURKISH CHILDREN AND ADOLESCENTS WITH NEW ONSET TYPE 1 DIABETES.

Journal.Title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology
